data.title: Build Process Lab HTMX flowsheet demo
Establish the flow-studio domain and SQLite repository
data.body:
## Goal
- Create the Go module, process-flow domain model, and SQLite-backed repository.
- Make one service own validation, persistence, and the caller-visible flow editing operations.

## Context
- The application is an educational single-user demo named Process Lab.
- Supported blocks are Source, Gain, First-order Lag, Sum, and Scope.
- A flow may branch and merge, but connections must remain acyclic.
- Block positions and parameters are persisted in SQLite.
- The service API exposes intent-revealing operations; HTTP handlers do not coordinate SQL transactions.
- Non-goals: authentication, collaboration, arbitrary user code, and production multi-tenancy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A seeded example flowsheet is created on first run.
- Blocks and connections round-trip through SQLite.
- Invalid block parameters, duplicate connections, type-invalid connections, and cycles are rejected.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./internal/studio`

data.title: Compile and simulate user-created flows
data.body:
## Goal
- Compile a persisted flow graph into a continuous-time state-space model and simulate it with `github.com/jamestjsp/controlsys`.

## Context
- Pin `controlsys` to stable `v1.2.0` and include its required Gonum fork replacement.
- The source block produces the external step input; gain and sum blocks are algebraic; lag blocks contribute dynamic states; scopes define plotted outputs.
- Graph compilation owns topological ordering and matrix construction.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Branched and merged acyclic graphs simulate on a uniform time grid.
- Simulation returns time-series data plus peak, final value, and settling indicators.
- Missing sources/scopes, cyclic graphs, and invalid lag constants return actionable errors.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./internal/studio -run 'TestSimulate|TestCompile'`

data.title: Build the HTMX process-flow workbench
data.body:
## Goal
- Deliver the server-rendered workbench and interactive editing endpoints.

## Context
- Use Go `html/template` and HTMX 2.0.10.
- HTMX owns server interactions and HTML fragment replacement.
- A small local JavaScript layer owns pointer dragging, connect-mode gestures, keyboard shortcuts, and SVG edge redraws because those are browser-local interactions.
- Return out-of-band fragments when one mutation affects the canvas, inspector, and status panels.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Users can add, select, configure, drag, connect, and delete blocks without full-page reloads.
- Users can run a simulation and receive an SVG trend plot plus metrics.
- The interface includes a palette, flowsheet canvas, properties inspector, status bar, and responsive small-screen behavior.
- Errors render inline and preserve the current workbench.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./internal/web`
- `go test ./...`

data.title: Document and verify the runnable demo
data.body:
## Goal
- Make the demo straightforward to run, inspect, and extend.

## Context
- Document architecture, HTMX interaction examples, SQLite location, supported block semantics, and controlsys integration.
- Keep all runtime assets embedded in the Go binary except the documented HTMX CDN script.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README includes prerequisites, run command, test command, interaction walkthrough, and architecture map.
- A clean build starts with a usable seeded flowsheet.
- Formatting, vet, tests, and production build pass.
- Browser validation covers add, drag, connect, edit, simulate, delete, refresh persistence, and responsive layout.

## Validation Gates
- `gofmt -w .`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./...`
- `go build ./cmd/processlab`
